name: cli
description: 📜 Entire CLI hooks into your Git workflow to capture AI agent sessions as you work. Sessions are indexed alongside commits, creating a searchable record of how code was written in your repo.
readmeExcerpt: # Entire CLI [Entire](https://entire.com) is a Git forge built for agent–human collaboration. This CLI is how you and your agents use Entire from the terminal — anything you do on entire.com, you can do here: - **Distributed Git hosting** — host repositories on Entire's Git-compatible server, or mirror your GitHub ones, and replicate them in regions around the world for data residency and the scale of agent traffic. → [Repositories & Git Hosting](#repositories--git-hosting) - **Trails** — instead of reviewing a diff, get a heads-up display for every change, with customizable evals that agents score on every push. → [Trails](#trails) - **Continuous memory** — capture every agent session as a checkpoint linked to your commits; [entire-brain](https://docs.entire.com/guides/brain/overview) combines them with [entire-graph](https://docs.entire.com/guides/graph/overview)'s code map into project memory. → [Agent Sessions](#agent-sessions) Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Antigravity, Factory AI Droid, Pi, and [more](https://docs.entire.com/agents/agent-integration-protocol/overview), and extends through [plugins](#plugins). Pushes through a GitHub mirror still trigger your GitHub Actions, and Trails can also show CI results from Buildkite and Depot. Open source under the MIT license. Docs: **[docs.entire.com](https://docs.entire.com)**. ## Contents - [Install](#install) - [Quick Start](#quick-start) - [Repositories & Git Hosting](#repositories--git-hosting) - [Trails](#trails) - [Agent Sessions](#agent-sessions) - [Search, Activity & the API](#search-activity--the-api) - [Plugins](#plugins) - [Security & Privacy](#security--privacy) - [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting) - [Documentation](#documentation) ## Install ```bash brew install --cask entireio/tap/entire # macOS and Linux curl -fsSL https://entire.com/install.sh | bash # macOS and Linux, without Homebrew irm https://entire.com/install.ps1 | iex # Windows PowerShell 5.1+ ``` For the nightly channel (prerelease builds with the latest changes): ```bash brew install --cask entireio/tap/entire@nightly curl -fsSL https://entire.com/install.sh | bash -s -- --channel nightly iex "& {$(irm https://entire.com/install.ps1)} -Channel nightly" ``` Requires Git on macOS, Linux, or Windows. Scoop, `go install`, and installing during a GitHub outage are covered in [Installation](https://docs.entire.com/installation). ## Quick Start **1. Capture agent sessions** — works in any Git repository, no account needed: ```bash cd your-project entire enable # pick your agents; installs their hooks and Entire's git hooks entire status # current sessions and where checkpoints are uploaded ``` **2. Put a repository on Entire** — sign in, then mirror a GitHub repository into one or more clusters, or create an Entire-native one. Mirroring needs the [Entire GitHub App](https://docs.entire.com/guides/repositories/github-app-access) installed for that repository. ```bash entire login entire repo mirror add # wizard: pick repos and clusters entire repo clone /gh// --nearest entire project create # wizard: owner, name, region entire repo create --project entire repo clone /et// ``` Then `cd` into the clone and run `entire enable` there to capture sessions in it. **3. Open a Trail** — in a repository on Entire, on the branch you're working on: ```bash git switch -c add-rate-limiting entire trail create --title "Add rate limiting" entire trail show ``` ## Repositories & Git Hosting Entire hosts Git repositories on clusters in several regions, so agents can clone, fetch, and push against a copy near where they run. - **Region** — where an organization's or project's data stays: a jurisdiction such as `us` or `eu`, set with `--region` when you create it. - **Cluster** — an Entire Git host, such as `aws-eu-central-1.entire.io`. `entire cluster list` shows them; a repository can have copies on several. - **Project** — holds Entire-native repositories and belongs to an organization or a personal account. Repository and project commands take its plain name (`--project acme`); Trail commands take `et/`, and treat a GitHub owner as the project for its mirrors (`gh/`). - **Mirror** — a copy of a repository on one cluster. GitHub repositories are mirrored from their GitHub upstream, and native repositories can be mirrored to more clusters. `entire repo mirror` manages both. Repository references name their forge: `/et//` for an Entire-native repository, `/gh//` for a GitHub mirror, or a full `entire:///…` clone URL. ```bash entire repo create web --project acme # Entire-native, private by default entire repo mirror add /gh/acme/web --cluster aws-us-east-2.entire.io,aws-eu-central-1.entire.io entire repo clone /gh/acme/web --nearest # time each cluster and use the fastest entire repo remote add entire # add Entire to an existing checkout, beside origin ``` A GitHub mirror keeps GitHub as the source of truth: clones and fetches come from Entire, and pushes are forwarded to GitHub, where your GitHub permissions, branch protection, and required checks still apply. Clones use `entire://` URLs through the `git-remote-entire` helper that ships with the packaged installs; after that, it is plain Git. See [Repositories](https://docs.entire.com/guides/repositories/overview) and [Mirrors in the CLI](https://docs.entire.com/guides/repositories/mirrors-in-cli) for regions, mirroring, unmirrored branches, moving a mirror off GitHub, branch protection, and access. ## Trails A **Trail** follows a change from intent to merge. Instead of reviewing a diff, you get a heads-up display for it — the Trail's page on entire.com, or `entire trail show` and `entire trail watch` here — with findings from evals that agents score on every push. Each Trail has a number in its project, such as `#42`. ```bash entire trail create --title "Add rate limiting" --type feature # publishes the current branch entire trail list --project et/acme --status open entire trail show # the Trail for the current branch entire trail watch # stream reviews, findings, and agent run events live entire trail finding # findings and each review agent's latest reading for this branch entire trail finding apply # apply a finding's suggested fix entire trail finding resolve -m "fixed in abc123" entire trail finding reply -m "intentional: the cache is per process" entire trail comment add -m "Should this cover the admin API too?" entire trail ready # mark this branch's change ready for review (--undo: back to draft) entire trail retarget --base release/2 # change the base branch it merges into entire trail attachment add shot.png # upload an image; prints the line that shows it in the description entire trail approve entire trail rerun-review # review the current head again (--agent for one agent) entire trail update-branch # merge the base into the branch on the server (Entire-native repos) entire trail merge # merge this branch's change into its base entire trail resume 42 # continue Trail #42: restore its branch's sessions in your agent ``` Trail commands use the current repository's project (`gh/` or `et/`); pass `--project` or `--repo` to work on another one without a checkout. `entire trail list` always takes `--project`. Other subcommands are `checkout`, `link`, `unlink`, `update`, and `approvals`. **Project agents** are those evals: review agents such as risk, confidence, drift, security, and review, configured per project in Entire, which score each push to a Trail and raise its findings. `entire project agent` lists them and adds Entire's presets to your repository with `add`; `entire project agent run` lists, inspects, cancels, and retries their runs. Preset agents run on free credit; a custom agent runs once the project's billing is set up. ## Agent Sessions `entire enable` connects your agents and installs Entire's git hooks, keeping any hooks you already have. Use your agent and commit as usual: each commit that includes agent work gets a **checkpoint** — the prompts, transcript, and files touched — linked to the commit by an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer. Entire never adds commits to your branch; by default, checkpoints are stored as their own Git refs (`refs/entire/checkpoints/…`) and pushed alongside your code. ```bash entire checkpoint list # checkpoints on this branch entire checkpoint explain # the prompt, transcript, and files behind a checkpoint entire session resume # restore a branch's sessions and continue in your agent entire agent add # add an agent later; entire configure for other settings entire disable # turn capture off (--uninstall removes Entire from the repo) ``` See [Sessions](https://docs.entire.com/guides/sessions/overview) and [Checkpoint Storage](https://docs.entire.com/guides/checkpoints/checkpoint-storage) for how capture works and migrating from legacy branch storage, [Settings](https://docs.entire.com/guides/configuration/settings-layers) and [Git Hooks](https://docs.entire.com/guides/configuration/git-hooks) for configuration, and [Checkpoint Destination](https://docs.entire.com/guides/checkpoints/checkpoint-destination) for choosing the remote or a [separate checkpoint repository](https://docs.entire.com/guides/checkpoints/store-checkpoints-in-another-repo). Checkpoints are also the raw material for continuous memory: [entire-brain](https://docs.entire.com/guides/brain/overview), installed separately, combines them with [entire-graph](https://docs.entire.com/guides/graph/overview)'s code map into project memory your agents can query. From the CLI, `entire search` and `entire checkpoint explain` are the way in. ## Search, Activity & the API - **Search** — `entire search` runs hybrid (semantic + keyword) search over checkpoints, commits, and sessions, scoped to the current repo or `--all-repos`. `--json --compact` returns a trimmed shape suited to agents, and `entire checkpoint explain ` fetches the full detail of a hit. - **Activity and dispatches** — `entire activity` shows your activity overview, repository breakdown, and recent sessions from entire.com. `entire dispatch` writes a summary of recent agent work; `--local` generates it with your locally installed agent CLI instead of the Entire server. - **Raw API access** — `entire api ` makes an authenticated request to an Entire API and prints the JSON response, like `gh api`. It attaches your token and picks the host: `--to core` (the default) reaches the control plane (orgs, projects, repos, mirrors, clusters), `--to cell` reaches your home data cell (activity, repo aggregates), and `--jurisdiction ` reaches another jurisdiction's cell. `{owner}`, `{repo}`, and `{repo_id}` in the path are filled from the current repository's `origin`; `{repo_id}` needs a GitHub repository with an active Entire mirror. These endpoints are internal and can change without notice; where a purpose-built command exists, prefer it. ```bash entire api /api/v1/clusters entire api --to cell "/api/v1/me/recap?repo={repo_id}" entire api /api/v1/me ``` ## Plugins Any executable named `entire-` on `$PATH` runs as `entire `. Install plugins from the [plugin index](https://github.com/entireio/plugin-index) or any Git host: ```bash entire plugin search entire plugin install entire plugin list ``` Installs from a Git host are verified against
readmeHtml:
Entire CLI

Entire is a Git forge built for agent–human collaboration. This CLI is how you and your agents use Entire from the terminal — anything you do on entire.com, you can do here:

  • Distributed Git hosting — host repositories on Entire's Git-compatible server, or mirror your GitHub ones, and replicate them in regions around the world for data residency and the scale of agent traffic. → Repositories & Git Hosting
  • Trails — instead of reviewing a diff, get a heads-up display for every change, with customizable evals that agents score on every push. → Trails
  • Continuous memory — capture every agent session as a checkpoint linked to your commits; entire-brain combines them with entire-graph's code map into project memory. → Agent Sessions

Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Antigravity, Factory AI Droid, Pi, and more, and extends through plugins. Pushes through a GitHub mirror still trigger your GitHub Actions, and Trails can also show CI results from Buildkite and Depot.

Open source under the MIT license. Docs: docs.entire.com.

Contents

  • Install
  • Quick Start
  • Repositories & Git Hosting
  • Trails
  • Agent Sessions
  • Search, Activity & the API
  • Plugins
  • Security & Privacy
  • Troubleshooting
  • Documentation

Install

brew install --cask entireio/tap/entire          # macOS and Linux
curl -fsSL https://entire.com/install.sh | bash  # macOS and Linux, without Homebrew
irm https://entire.com/install.ps1 | iex         # Windows PowerShell 5.1+

For the nightly channel (prerelease builds with the latest changes):

brew install --cask entireio/tap/entire@nightly
curl -fsSL https://entire.com/install.sh | bash -s -- --channel nightly
iex "& {$(irm https://entire.com/install.ps1)} -Channel nightly"

Requires Git on macOS, Linux, or Windows. Scoop, go install, and installing during a GitHub outage are covered in Installation.

Quick Start

1. Capture agent sessions — works in any Git repository, no account needed:

cd your-project
entire enable                    # pick your agents; installs their hooks and Entire's git hooks
entire status                    # current sessions and where checkpoints are uploaded

2. Put a repository on Entire — sign in, then mirror a GitHub repository into one or more clusters, or create an Entire-native one. Mirroring needs the Entire GitHub App installed for that repository.

entire login

entire repo mirror add                          # wizard: pick repos and clusters
entire repo clone /gh/<owner>/<repo> --nearest

entire project create                           # wizard: owner, name, region
entire repo create <name> --project <project>
entire repo clone /et/<project>/<name>

Then cd into the clone and run entire enable there to capture sessions in it.

3. Open a Trail — in a repository on Entire, on the branch you're working on:

git switch -c add-rate-limiting
entire trail create --title "Add rate limiting"
entire trail show

Repositories & Git Hosting

Entire hosts Git repositories on clusters in several regions, so agents can clone, fetch, and push against a copy near where they run.

  • Region — where an organization's or project's data stays: a jurisdiction such as us or eu, set with --region when you create it.
  • Cluster — an Entire Git host, such as aws-eu-central-1.entire.io. entire cluster list shows them; a repository can have copies on several.
  • Project — holds Entire-native repositories and belongs to an organization or a personal account. Repository and project commands take its plain name (--project acme); Trail commands take et/<project>, and treat a GitHub owner as the project for its mirrors (gh/<owner>).
  • Mirror — a copy of a repository on one cluster. GitHub repositories are mirrored from their GitHub upstream, and native repositories can be mirrored to more clusters. entire repo mirror manages both.

Repository references name their forge: /et/<project>/<repo> for an Entire-native repository, /gh/<owner>/<repo> for a GitHub mirror, or a full entire://<cluster>/… clone URL.

entire repo create web --project acme                   # Entire-native, private by default
entire repo mirror add /gh/acme/web --cluster aws-us-east-2.entire.io,aws-eu-central-1.entire.io
entire repo clone /gh/acme/web --nearest                # time each cluster and use the fastest
entire repo remote add entire                           # add Entire to an existing checkout, beside origin

A GitHub mirror keeps GitHub as the source of truth: clones and fetches come from Entire, and pushes are forwarded to GitHub, where your GitHub permissions, branch protection, and required checks still apply. Clones use entire:// URLs through the git-remote-entire helper that ships with the packaged installs; after that, it is plain Git.

See Repositories and Mirrors in the CLI for regions, mirroring, unmirrored branches, moving a mirror off GitHub, branch protection, and access.

Trails

A Trail follows a change from intent to merge. Instead of reviewing a diff, you get a heads-up display for it — the Trail's page on entire.com, or entire trail show and entire trail watch here — with findings from evals that agents score on every push. Each Trail has a number in its project, such as #42.

entire trail create --title "Add rate limiting" --type feature   # publishes the current branch
entire trail list --project et/acme --status open
entire trail show                       # the Trail for the current branch
entire trail watch                      # stream reviews, findings, and agent run events live

entire trail finding                    # findings and each review agent's latest reading for this branch
entire trail finding apply <id>         # apply a finding's suggested fix
entire trail finding resolve <id> -m "fixed in abc123"
entire trail finding reply <id> -m "intentional: the cache is per process"

entire trail comment add -m "Should this cover the admin API too?"
entire trail ready                      # mark this branch's change ready for review (--undo: back to draft)
entire trail retarget --base release/2  # change the base branch it merges into
entire trail attachment add shot.png    # upload an image; prints the line that shows it in the description
entire trail approve
entire trail rerun-review               # review the current head again (--agent <id> for one agent)
entire trail update-branch              # merge the base into the branch on the server (Entire-native repos)
entire trail merge                      # merge this branch's change into its base
entire trail resume 42                  # continue Trail #42: restore its branch's sessions in your agent

Trail commands use the current repository's project (gh/<owner> or et/<project>); pass --project or --repo to work on another one without a checkout. entire trail list always takes --project. Other subcommands are checkout, link, unlink, update, and approvals.

Project agents are those evals: review agents such as risk, confidence, drift, security, and review, configured per project in Entire, which score each push to a Trail and raise its findings. entire project agent lists them and adds Entire's presets to your repository with add; entire project agent run lists, inspects, cancels, and retries their runs. Preset agents run on free credit; a custom agent runs once the project's billing is set up.

Agent Sessions

entire enable connects your agents and installs Entire's git hooks, keeping any hooks you already have. Use your agent and commit as usual: each commit that includes agent work gets a checkpoint — the prompts, transcript, and files touched — linked to the commit by an Entire-Checkpoint trailer. Entire never adds commits to your branch; by default, checkpoints are stored as their own Git refs (refs/entire/checkpoints/…) and pushed alongside your code.

entire checkpoint list                # checkpoints on this branch
entire checkpoint explain <id>        # the prompt, transcript, and files behind a checkpoint
entire session resume <branch>        # restore a branch's sessions and continue in your agent
entire agent add <name>               # add an agent later; entire configure for other settings
entire disable                        # turn capture off (--uninstall removes Entire from the repo)

See Sessions and Checkpoint Storage for how capture works and migrating from legacy branch storage, Settings and Git Hooks for configuration, and Checkpoint Destination for choosing the remote or a separate checkpoint repository.

Checkpoints are also the raw material for continuous memory: entire-brain, installed separately, combines them with entire-graph's code map into project memory your agents can query. From the CLI, entire search and entire checkpoint explain are the way in.

Search, Activity & the API

  • Search — entire search runs hybrid (semantic + keyword) search over checkpoints, commits, and sessions, scoped to the current repo or --all-repos. --json --compact returns a trimmed shape suited to agents, and entire checkpoint explain <id> fetches the full detail of a hit.
  • Activity and dispatches — entire activity shows your activity overview, repository breakdown, and recent sessions from entire.com. entire dispatch writes a summary of recent agent work; --local generates it with your locally installed agent CLI instead of the Entire server.
  • Raw API access — entire api <path> makes an authenticated request to an Entire API and prints the JSON response, like gh api. It attaches your token and picks the host: --to core (the default) reaches the control plane (orgs, projects, repos, mirrors, clusters), --to cell reaches your home data cell (activity, repo aggregates), and --jurisdiction <slug> reaches another jurisdiction's cell. {owner}, {repo}, and {repo_id} in the path are filled from the current repository's origin; {repo_id} needs a GitHub repository with an active Entire mirror. These endpoints are internal and can change without notice; where a purpose-built command exists, prefer it.
entire api /api/v1/clusters
entire api --to cell "/api/v1/me/recap?repo={repo_id}"
entire api /api/v1/me

Plugins

Any executable named entire-<name> on $PATH runs as entire <name>. Install plugins from the plugin index or any Git host:

entire plugin search
entire plugin install <name>
entire plugin list

Installs from a Git host are verified against the release's checksums.txt. See entire plugin.

Security & Privacy

Session transcripts are pushed to your Git remote — as checkpoint refs, not commits on your branch. If that repository is public, anyone can read them. Entire redacts detected secrets before writing a checkpoint, but redaction is best effort; entire checkpoint list --outgoing shows what your next push will upload, and entire checkpoint explain <id> shows a checkpoint's contents.

To keep transcripts out of a public repository, upload them to a separate private repository (entire configure --local --checkpoint-remote github:<owner>/<repo>) or stop uploading them (entire configure --local --skip-push-sessions). entire enable names the checkpoint destination every time it runs. See Security for redaction, scanners, deleting checkpoints, and cleaning up data from older versions.

Troubleshooting

Issue Solution
"Not a git repository" Navigate to a Git repository first
"Entire is disabled" Run entire enable
Agent hooks outdated after a CLI upgrade Run entire agent add <name>; add --force if that does not fix them
A session stuck ACTIVE, or leftover session state Run entire doctor, then entire clean --force if it persists
Anything else Run entire doctor; entire doctor bundle produces a redacted diagnostic bundle for a bug report

Set ENTIRE_LOG_LEVEL=debug for debug logs, and ACCESSIBLE=1 for screen-reader-friendly prompts. Headless servers and CI: see entire login.

Documentation

  • docs.entire.com — guides for Entire and the CLI, including how the CLI and entire.com fit together
  • entire help, entire <command> --help, and the CLI reference; entire agent-help is the version written for coding agents
  • Issues: https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues · Contributing: CONTRIBUTING.md

License

MIT License — see LICENSE.

releases.name: v0.13.1
releases.body:
### Added

- Checkpoint push policy: each clone can keep checkpoints local until you send them. `automatic`, the default, keeps today's behavior. Under `manual`, `git push` uploads no checkpoints and pre-push prints how many are waiting; `entire checkpoint push <id>[@<commit>]` or `--all` uploads them. On the first terminal push with checkpoints waiting, Entire asks once whether to push automatically, manually, or decide later (it waits 60s and backs off for 7 days on timeout). A policy that can't be read uploads nothing. `manual` is not supported on the git-branch backend ([#2921](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2921), [#2936](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2936), [#3008](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/3008))
- OpenCode 2 support, with the same coverage as OpenCode 1, which keeps working. The plugin moves to `.opencode/plugin/entire.ts` ([#2854](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2854))

aiSummary.oneLiner: A Git-native CLI tool that indexes AI agent sessions alongside commits for full traceability.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: The Entire CLI integrates directly with your Git workflow to capture and index the complete history of AI agent interactions during development. It records prompts, responses, files touched, and token usage, attaching this rich metadata directly to your standard Git commits. This allows developers to instantly understand the context of why code changed, rather than just seeing the final output. The tool also provides mechanisms to rewind to specific checkpoints if an autonomous agent generates incorrect code, keeping the main Git history perfectly clean. It supports major models and agents like Claude Code and Codex out of the box.
keyFeatures: Session indexing: Captures complete prompt transcripts and links them directly to the corresponding Git commit.
Instant rollback: Allows developers to rewind the codebase to a known-good state if an AI agent goes off track.
Context preservation: Maintains a searchable, versioned record of every AI interaction for future onboarding and audits.
Zero context switching: Operates entirely within the terminal and standard Git workflows without requiring external dashboards.
Broad compatibility: Works natively with various AI coding assistants including Claude Code, Gemini, and Codex.

useCases.title: Codebase auditing
useCases.description: Review the exact prompts and tool calls an AI used to generate a specific, complex pull request.

useCases.title: Agent error recovery
useCases.description: Quickly reverting changes when an autonomous coding agent misunderstands instructions and corrupts multiple files.

useCases.title: Developer onboarding
useCases.description: Allow new team members to read the AI session transcripts to understand the reasoning behind legacy architectural choices.

useCases.title: Compliance tracking
useCases.description: Maintain a verifiable trail of how AI was used to generate or modify sensitive production code.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Software engineers and teams who extensively use AI coding assistants and need robust traceability, auditability, and rollback capabilities integrated directly into their existing version control workflows. Familiarity with agents workflows is highly recommended for optimal usage.
